evidence_policy: peer-reviewed primary papers with official proceedings or publisher records

sources.title: Audit Games
sources.venue: Twenty-Third International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
sources.claim_used: Audit allocation and punishment are modeled as a defender-auditee Stackelberg game.
sources.transfer_limit: Hospital and bank audit motivations do not validate an AI model-release game.

sources.title: Audit Games with Multiple Defender Resources
sources.venue: Twenty-Ninth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
sources.claim_used: The audit-game model is generalized to multiple restricted resources and an FPTAS is provided for that model.
sources.transfer_limit: The algorithm applies only to its specified action and utility model.

sources.title: On the Inducibility of Stackelberg Equilibrium for Security Games
sources.venue: Thirty-Third AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
sources.claim_used: Favorable follower tie-breaking in strong Stackelberg equilibrium can overstate guaranteed defender utility.
sources.transfer_limit: The paper does not select an MRAP equilibrium concept.

sources.title: Security Games with Limited Surveillance
sources.venue: Twenty-Sixth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
sources.claim_used: Costly limited surveillance can replace perfect observation of the defender strategy.
sources.evidence_location: official AAAI abstract and issue record
sources.transfer_limit: The surveillance model is not calibrated for model attacks.

sources.title: PROTECT: An Application of Computational Game Theory for the Security of the Ports of the United States
sources.venue: Twenty-Sixth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
sources.claim_used: A Stackelberg security-game system using quantal response was deployed for United States Coast Guard patrol scheduling.
sources.transfer_limit: The deployed behavioral model does not transfer automatically to MRAP attackers.

sources.title: Strategic Classification
sources.claim_used: Classifier choice and costly strategic feature response are modeled as a sequential game.
sources.transfer_limit: Strategic model users are not automatically equivalent to release submitters or attackers.

sources.title: Strategic Classification is Causal Modeling in Disguise
sources.venue: Thirty-Seventh International Conference on Machine Learning
sources.claim_used: Interpreting strategic adaptations and designing incentive cost functions can require causal identification.
sources.transfer_limit: The paper does not identify MRAP-specific causal primitives.

sources.title: Performative Prediction
sources.venue: Thirty-Seventh International Conference on Machine Learning
sources.claim_used: Deployment can change future data distributions and performative stability is a distinct equilibrium notion.
sources.transfer_limit: Stability conditions require a registered response map.

sources.title: Learning to Incentivize Information Acquisition: Proper Scoring Rules Meet Principal-Agent Model
sources.venue: Fortieth International Conference on Machine Learning
sources.claim_used: Costly information acquisition is modeled as a principal-agent Stackelberg interaction using scoring rules.
sources.transfer_limit: The online scoring-rule result is not an MRAP assessor contract.

sources.title: Active fairness auditing
sources.venue: Thirty-Ninth International Conference on Machine Learning
sources.claim_used: A provider can change a model after audit queries while remaining consistent with observed answers; the paper defines a manipulation-proof estimation problem.
sources.evidence_location: official paper introduction and PMLR metadata
sources.transfer_limit: Fairness-query estimation does not establish general release safety.

sources.title: Trustless Audits without Revealing Data or Models
sources.venue: Forty-First International Conference on Machine Learning
sources.claim_used: Commitments and zero-knowledge proofs are combined to audit specified properties without revealing the model or data in the paper's protocol.
sources.transfer_limit: Cryptographic consistency does not establish evidence adequacy or incentive compatibility.

sources.title: Closing the AI accountability gap: defining an end-to-end framework for internal algorithmic auditing
sources.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency
sources.claim_used: Internal algorithmic auditing is organized across the development lifecycle with retained documentation.
sources.transfer_limit: The process framework is not an equilibrium or deterrence proof.

non_claim: The ledger verifies citation provenance and claim scope; it does not prove source correctness, external validity, or transfer to a deployment.
